entries.04fe400681d50fcb: These are production and sales in Japan, undertaken by the company and its domestic consolidated subsidiaries. In addition to four company-owned plants, the Shizuoka Plant, Haibara Plant, Sagara Plant and Fujikawa Machinery Plant, subsidiaries including Koito Kyushu Co., Ltd. and Aoitec Co., Ltd. manufacture automotive lighting. Koito Denko Co., Ltd. handles railway vehicle control equipment, road traffic signals and traffic control systems, railway vehicle seats and so on, and the transport services of Koito Unso Co., Ltd. and the insurance agency business of Koito Insurance Service Co., Ltd. also fall into this segment. The largest customer is TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION, and its sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥128,481 million (13.6% of total sales). Revenue in this segment for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥367.8 billion, up 4.6% from the previous year, due to new orders and higher sales of the company's ordered vehicle models.

entries.37a1308fb114e4d0: The group consists of KOITO MANUFACTURING CO., LTD. and its subsidiaries, affiliates and other affiliated companies. Its principal operations are the manufacture and sale of automotive lighting, aircraft parts, railway vehicle parts and various electrical equipment, and related logistics. The reportable [[term:segment|segments]] are five by location: Japan, the Americas, China, Asia and Europe, and the company has production sites in 11 countries worldwide. The number of employees as of the end of March 2026 was 21,507 (excluding average temporary employees of 3,142). [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] holds 21% of the voting rights and is an [[term:other-affiliated-company|other affiliated company]].

entries.63c4dd066c5578fa: Automotive lighting is mostly for assembly by automakers. The company receives tentative production plans for designated models from each customer 2 to 3 months in advance, sets its production outlook accordingly, and delivers to the line on instructions timed to the automaker's next-day or ten-day schedule. As tentative plans and actual figures can differ, the company states that it is difficult to calculate order volume and order backlog. Replacement parts are produced on a forecast basis according to sales plans. The customer that appears in sales by customer is [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]], with sales of ¥128,481 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (13.6% of total sales; previous year ¥119,571 million, 13.0%), and the related segment is Japan. Sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026, by customer location, were ¥361,325 million in Japan, ¥332,809 million in the Americas (of which the United States ¥249,395 million), ¥60,203 million in China, ¥156,684 million in Asia and ¥36,586 million in Europe.
entries.63d58ac75a08b168: The core products are automotive lighting, such as LED headlamps, headlamps and auxiliary lamps, marker lamps and high-mount stop lamps.
entries.688680debee631b5: Sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥947,610 million (¥947.6 billion), up 3.4% from the prior year. The company explains that, in addition to new orders in each region, sales of its ordered models increased due to higher demand for hybrid vehicles in the Americas and sales promotion campaigns by customers. By regional segment, sales to external customers were: Japan ¥367,826 million (up 4.6% year on year), the Americas ¥328,641 million (up 4.3%), Asia ¥162,683 million (up 4.6%), China ¥53,332 million (down 8.5%), and Europe ¥35,125 million (down 2.9%). The reasons for the decline in China are the continued weak sales of Japanese-brand vehicles, which account for a high proportion of the company's sales, and in Europe the effect of the transfer of all shares in its UK subsidiary in November 2025. From the current period, the former 'North America' and 'Other' have been combined into 'Americas', and segment information for the prior period has also been restated under the new categories.
entries.68e6dbbb580da9c5: The core products are automotive lighting, such as LED headlamps, headlamps and auxiliary lamps, marker lamps and high-mount stop lamps. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥886,039 million for the automotive lighting business, ¥40,799 million for the non-automotive lighting and electrical equipment business, and ¥20,771 million for other business. Other products include railway vehicle control equipment, road traffic signals and traffic control systems, road and tunnel lighting, aircraft parts and electronic components, and railway vehicle seats. The company outsources development of LiDAR-related technology to Cepton Technologies, Inc. of the United States. Future challenges cited include expanding the adoption of ADB (variable light distribution headlamps), which contribute to reducing traffic accidents, and communication lamps compatible with next-generation transport infrastructure.
entries.6cdc47f06a53bfba: Koito Czech s.r.o. in the Czech Republic manufactures and sells automotive lighting for the European market. In November 2025, the company transferred all shares of Koito Europe Limited (United Kingdom) to Shapers’Group Limited and excluded it from the scope of consolidation, so it has also been removed from the table of business details and the business structure diagram. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥35.1 billion, down 2.9% from the previous year, partly reflecting the effect of the transfer of the UK subsidiary.

entries.aaae9df400b254db: Its strategies include: strengthening its five-region global structure of Japan, the Americas, Europe, China and Asia under the corporate message 'Entrusting Safety to Light'; responding to changes in mobility such as connectivity, autonomous driving, sharing and electrification; pursuing high quality and safety while strengthening environmental conservation and compliance; and strengthening its earnings structure and corporate base through securing and effectively using management resources. As priority issues, under 'KOITO VISION ～Illuminating the Future of People and the Earth～', the company is working on 'strengthening the corporate foundation', 'sustainable growth' and 'coexistence with the Earth and society', and aims to reduce CO2 emissions in fiscal 2030 by 50% compared with fiscal 2015 and achieve carbon neutrality in fiscal 2050.

(Malaysia) manufacture and sell automotive lighting. entries.fb89bff0329946ee: These are production and sales in the United States, Mexico and Brazil. North American Lighting, Inc. (Illinois, United States), North American Lighting Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (Mexico), and NAL do Brasil Indústria e Comércio de Componentes de Iluminação Ltda. (Brazil) manufacture and sell automotive lighting. North American Lighting, Inc. is a specified subsidiary whose revenue exceeds 10% of consolidated revenue. Cepton Technologies, Inc., a U.S. company responsible for developing LiDAR-related technology, also falls into this segment. From the current period, the company has combined the former 'North America' and 'Other' into 'Americas'. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥328.6 billion, up 4.3% from the previous year, due to stronger demand for hybrid vehicles and higher sales of the company's ordered vehicle models linked to customer sales promotion campaigns.
